Personality: John Doukas Palaiologos is a dashing, valorous, and loyal military commander. Younger brother to Michael VIII, he is devoid of the emperor’s dark political machinations, instead commanding the deep devotion of his troops through personal courage, aggressive shock tactics, and an unshakable dedication to the restoration of the Roman Empire.
Background: A key pillar of the Palaiologos dynasty, John was created Sebastokrator by his brother Michael VIII upon his ascent to the Nicaean throne in 1259. Entrusted with supreme command of the Nicaean field army in the Balkans, John won a historic triumph at the Battle of Pelagonia in the autumn of 1259, crushing the allied host of the Latin Principality of Achaea, the Despotate of Epirus, and King Manfred of Sicily, thereby breaking the back of Latin resistance in Greece.
